identity.name: Duchy of Modena and Reggio
alt_names: Duchy of Modena, Reggio and Mirandola

land.text: the Duchy of Modena and Reggio re-established when the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy was dissolved

predecessors.note: Modena page: 'With the dissolution of the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy in 1814, Francis IV assumed rule as Duke of Modena'; infobox 'Re-established: 1814'. The duchy itself was 'Created: 1452' and 'Conquered by France: 1796' (infobox); the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy has no dossier yet.

land.text: 'In December, Modena joined with Tuscany and Parma to form the' United Provinces of Central Italy

successors.note: The united provinces were 'annexed to the growing Kingdom of Sardinia in March 1860' (Modena page).

rulers.name: Francesco IV
rulers.note: 'Francis IV assumed rule as Duke of Modena' in 1814; the end year is the start of Francesco V in the infobox ('Francesco V (1846-1859)').

rulers.name: Francesco V
rulers.note: Last duke; infobox 'Francesco V (1846-1859)'; 'forced to flee, this time permanently' during the war of April to July 1859.

correction.text: the duchy as restored in 1814-15: Cliopatria's 1815 shape without Guastalla (Parma's until 17 December 1847) and Fivizzano (Tuscan until 1847); the Lunigiana fiefs (December 1815) and Massa and Carrara (1829) arrive by ledger event

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Modena shape begins in 1815 but the page re-establishes the duchy in 1814. The shape is Cliopatria's 1815 outline without Guastalla and Fivizzano, which the Treaty of Florence page gives to Modena only at Marie Louise's death on 17 December 1847.

correction.text: the duchy as restored in 1814-15: Cliopatria's 1815 shape without Guastalla (Parma's until 17 December 1847) and Fivizzano (Tuscan until 1847); the Lunigiana fiefs (December 1815) and Massa and Carrara (1829) arrive by ledger event

keyframe_review.note: 6,816 km2 for 1815-1847. The Treaty of Florence page: 'Parma, in turn, ceded the former Duchy of Guastalla to Modena' and Fivizzano went to Modena, both taking effect on 17 December 1847, so a shape that holds Guastalla and Fivizzano from 1815 is too large before then. Massa and Carrara joined in 1829 (ledger); Cliopatria's 1815-1847 outline does not show them and its 1849 outline does. The Modena page gives no area, so the infobox comparison cannot be made (population 238,000 in 1846 only).

7,097 km2 for 1849-1858: the duchy after the 1847 exchanges, with Guastalla, Fivizzano and Massa-Carrara. Consistent with the Treaty of Florence page (Guastalla, Fivizzano, Massa and Carrara all Modenese). No area on the Modena page to compare.

correction.text: the 1849-1858 outline unchanged to the duchy's end in December 1859

keyframe_review.note: 6,816 km2 for 1859, the 1815 outline again (the Carrara cell of the 1849 shape is missing). No page opened records Modena losing land before 'December 1859'; the duke fled 'permanently' during the war of April to July 1859 but the duchy's land stayed Modenese until it joined the United Provinces.

correction.text: the 1849 outline, for the year of the revolution

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Modena shape for 1848. The page says the Austria-Este dukes 'were briefly ousted in the revolutions of 1831 and 1848, but soon returned', so the duchy continues in law; the shape is the 1849 outline (Guastalla and Fivizzano were Modenese from 17 December 1847).

region.text: the duchy as restored in 1814-15: Cliopatria's 1815 shape without Guastalla (Parma's until 17 December 1847) and Fivizzano (Tuscan until 1847); the Lunigiana fiefs (December 1815) and Massa and Carrara (1829) arrive by ledger event

ledger.note: 1814: Francis IV re-establishes the Duchy of Modena and Reggio as the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy dissolves. 'With the dissolution of the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy in 1814, Francis IV assumed rule as Duke of Modena'; infobox 'Re-established: 1814'. The page gives no month; the Final Act of 9 June 1815 'acknowledged' Francis IV 'as the ruler of the Duchy of Modena, Reggio and Mirandola' (Congress of Vienna page).

region.text: the former imperial fiefs in Lunigiana

ledger.note: December 1815: Francis IV takes the Este fiefs in Lunigiana from his mother. 'In December 1815 he obtained the transfer from his mother Maria Beatrice d'Este of the former imperial fiefs in Lunigiana', fiefs 'not reconstituted by the Congress of Vienna'. The page does not list the fiefs; the region is the whole of Lunigiana as the nearest name. Reviewer eu-20-j: confidence lowered from 3 to 2 because the page names Lunigiana but not the fiefs, and the whole region overstates them.

region.text: the Duchy of Massa and Carrara

ledger.note: 1829: Modena inherits Massa and Carrara. 'On her death in 1829, he also inherited the Duchy of Massa and Carrara'; the Treaty of Florence page agrees: 'in 1829, the Duchy of Massa and Carrara was annexed by the Duchy of Modena and Reggio'.

17 December 1847: Guastalla passes from Parma to Modena. 'Parma, in turn, ceded the former Duchy of Guastalla to Modena'; the treaty took effect 'Upon the death of Marie Louise, Duchess of Parma, Piacenza, and Guastalla (occurred on 17 December 1847)'.

1847: Fivizzano passes from Tuscany to Modena. The Treaty of Florence page: 'Tuscany agreed to transfer all its Lunigiana enclaves except Fivizzano', which the page says stayed Tuscan while Modena annexed it (paraphrase); no day is given for Fivizzano, so December is the treaty's effective date, not the page's own word for it. grand-duchy-of-tuscany records the loss in 1847.

December 1859: Modena joins the United Provinces of Central Italy. 'In December, Modena joined with Tuscany and Parma to form the' United Provinces; infobox 'Merged into the United Provinces of Central Italy: 1859'. Francis V had 'again' fled 'permanently' during the war of April to July 1859.

wars.name: Revolutions of 1831 and 1848 (Modena)
wars.outcome: The dukes 'were briefly ousted in the revolutions of 1831 and 1848, but soon returned'; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The page gives no months or places for either revolution.

wars.name: Second Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Francis V 'was again forced to flee, this time permanently' (war 'April to July 1859'); Modena joined the United Provinces of Central Italy in December 1859 and Sardinia in March 1860.
wars.note: The duchy's own land was not fought over on the page; the war is listed because it ended the state.

certainty.note: Frontiers with Parma, Tuscany and the Papal States were fixed by the Final Act (9 June 1815) and the 1844 Treaty of Florence; Cliopatria's outlines are coarse (one H3 cell, about 250 km2, of error).

notes: Reviewer eu-20-j: the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy is dossier italian-republic (1802-1814, alt name Kingdom of Italy (Napoleonic)); predecessor and found counterpart changed from kingdom-of-italy-napoleonic to it. Written from the Modena article and the Treaty of Florence page (page budget 1-2); the Congress of Vienna page is cited in one note. Cliopatria's 1815-1847 shape already holds Guastalla and Fivizzano (probed against the gazetteer), which Modena received only on 17 December 1847, and lacks Carrara until the 1849 shape; the keyframe corrections subtract the two and the ledger adds them back on the dates the pages give. The Cliopatria row has no 1848 shape (new keyframe 1848). Unverified here: the Neapolitan occupation of Modena in April 1815 (kingdom-of-naples-napoleonic carries it; no opened page mentions it), the Austrian garrison after 1849, and Modena's 1848 vote on union with Sardinia (kingdom-of-sardinia's ledger names it). Gazetteer names needed: places Guastalla, Fivizzano, Massa (Italy), Carrara; region Lunigiana. Counterparts without a dossier: duchy-of-massa-and-carrara (Maria Beatrice d'Este, restored 1815 per the Congress page, annexed 1829).
